items.statement:
Assume AC and Countable Choice and the finite-dimensional linear contextual bandit model. Put $S_t=\sum_{s=1}^tA_s\eta_s$, $G_t=\sum_{s=1}^tA_sA_s^{\mathsf T}$, and $V_t=\lambda I_d+G_t$. Let $\mathcal H_t:=\mathcal F_{t+1}$ be the information after round $t$ has been observed. Then

$$Z_t:=\sqrt{\frac{\det(V_0)}{\det(V_t)}}\exp\!\left(\frac12 S_t^{\mathsf T}V_t^{-1}S_t\right),\qquad Z_0:=1,$$

is a nonnegative integrable supermartingale with respect to $(\mathcal H_t)_{t=0}^n$.

items.title: LinUCB with a self-normalized confidence radius
items.statement:
**Inputs and admissibility.** Take the finite-dimensional linear contextual bandit model and a confidence level $\delta\in(0,1)$. At each round, the nonempty available action set is finite and ordered with its feature vectors, or the available feature set is compact with a supplied attained measurable predictable maximizer for the score below. In the finite case evaluate the score for each action's feature and resolve ties by the first action. All model assumptions, including $\lambda>0$, the feature and parameter bounds, pre-reward information, and the conditional noise bound, are in force.

**Outputs.** Before each reward is observed, output the selected feature $A_t$; after the reward $X_t$ is observed, record it. At the horizon return the online sequence $(A_t,X_t)_{t=1}^n$ and terminal state $(V_n,b_n,\widehat\theta_n)$.

Initialize $V_0=\lambda I_d$, $b_0=0$, $\widehat\theta_0=0$, $W_0=\lambda^{-1}I_d$, and $D_0=\lambda^d$. At each round $t=1,\ldots,n$, compute

$$\rho_t=\sqrt\lambda\,m_2+\sqrt{2\log(1/\delta)+\log(D_{t-1}/D_0)},\qquad \beta_t=\max\{1,\rho_t^2\},$$

Next select an available feature vector

$$A_t\in\arg\max_{a\in\mathcal A_t}\left\{\langle\widehat\theta_{t-1},a\rangle+\sqrt{\beta_t}\,\sqrt{a^{\mathsf T}W_{t-1}a}\right\}.$$

For a finite ordered action set, evaluate every action's score and take the first maximizing action's feature; for a compact feature set, call the supplied selector once. After observing reward $X_t$, update

$$V_t=V_{t-1}+A_tA_t^{\mathsf T},\qquad b_t=b_{t-1}+A_tX_t.$$

Then compute the updated matrix state $W_t,D_t$ from $V_t$ by the following exact row procedure. Form the augmented matrix $M=[V_t\mid I_d]$, set $s=1$ and $D=1$, and for $k=0,\ldots,d-1$ choose the least row index $i\ge k$ whose current left-block entry $M_{ik}$ is nonzero. If no such row exists, return failure. If $i\ne k$, swap rows $i$ and $k$ and replace $s$ by $-s$. Set $p_k=M_{kk}$, replace $D$ by $Dp_k$, divide row $k$ by $p_k$, and for every $j\ne k$ set $\operatorname{row}_j\leftarrow\operatorname{row}_j-M_{jk}\operatorname{row}_k$. After the loop set $W_t$ to the right block and $D_t=sD$, and set $\widehat\theta_t=W_tb_t$. For a compact feature set the supplied selector must return an attained maximizing feature measurably from pre-reward information.

items.title: The ridge estimate lies in a time-uniform linear confidence ellipsoid
LinUCB has a log-determinant high-probability pseudo-regret bound
items.statement:
Assume AC and Countable Choice, the finite-dimensional linear contextual bandit model, and LinUCB with $\beta_t=\max\{1,\rho_t^2\}$ as defined in the algorithm. Let $\delta\in(0,1)$ be the confidence input to LinUCB. Suppose also that for every round $t$,

$$\sup_{a,b\in\mathcal A_t}\langle\theta^*,a-b\rangle\le1.$$

Define the random pseudo-regret by

$$\widehat R_n:=\sum_{t=1}^n\left(\max_{a\in\mathcal A_t}\langle\theta^*,a\rangle-\langle\theta^*,A_t\rangle\right).$$

Then, with probability at least $1-\delta$,

$$\widehat R_n\le\sqrt{8n\beta_n\log\!\left(\frac{\det V_n}{\det V_0}\right)}\le\sqrt{8dn\beta_n\log\!\left(1+\frac{nL^2}{d\lambda}\right)}.$$

**Algorithm properties.** For every admissible model input, the algorithm also completes exactly $n$ rounds and outputs $(A_t,X_t)_{t=1}^n$ and $(V_n,b_n,\widehat\theta_n)$. Count exact real arithmetic operations, comparisons, square roots, and logarithms with unit cost, and exclude generation of contexts, features, and rewards. Let $F$ be the rounds with finite action sets and let $m_t$ be the number of available actions at round $t\in F$; let $K$ be the compact-feature rounds. The procedure makes exactly $|K|$ calls to the supplied maximizing selector and uses $O(nd^3+d^2\sum_{t\in F}m_t)$ operations apart from selector costs.

items.title: LinUCB has expected pseudo-regret of order $d\sqrt n\log(nL)$
items.statement:
Assume the hypotheses of the LinUCB high-probability regret theorem, with $d\ge1$, $\lambda>0$, $L\ge1$, $m_2\ge0$, and horizon $n\ge2$. Run LinUCB with $\delta=1/n$. Let $\widehat R_n$ be its random pseudo-regret and define expected pseudo-regret by $R_n:=\mathbb E[\widehat R_n]$. Put

$$q_n:=\log\!\left(1+\frac{nL^2}{d\lambda}\right),\qquad B_n:=\sqrt{8dn\beta_nq_n},$$

where $\beta_n$ is the algorithm's confidence schedule, and set

$$c:=1+\frac{\log(1+L/\lambda)}{\log2},\qquad C_1:=4+2c+\frac{1+2\lambda m_2^2}{\log2},\qquad C:=\sqrt{8C_1c}+\frac{1}{\sqrt2\log2}.$$

Here $B_n$ is generally random through $\beta_n$ and the design matrix. Then

$$R_n\le\mathbb E[B_n]+1\le C\,d\sqrt n\log(nL).$$

This is an expected pseudo-regret bound; it is distinct from a high-probability bound on realized reward regret.
